newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya opens its first private bank.
newsitem.headline: Libya opens its first private bank.

text.p: Libya has opened its first private bank, the Misratah Domestic Bank for Development and Investment, state-run Libyan television reported over the weekend.
The television, monitored in Tunis, said the bank had nine million Libyan dinars ($24.66 million) in capital. It gave no details on shareholders.

The bank, set up in Misratah, 150 km (90 miles) east of Tripoli, was the first of a series of banks which Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi last year ordered to be set up to channel resources to help finance local development projects.

The Misratah Bank opened its first bank account in the name of Muammar Gaddafi and credited it with 1969 Libyan dinars ($5,136), representing the year Gaddafi launched his revolution, Libyan television said.
